title: introduce-attribute-whitelist-shield-and-kms-context-prober
author: Mariana Cortez
description:
Context and motivation:
Some enterprise customers require tighter RBAC controls along with stronger evidence that keys and crypto operations are region-bound. This PR introduces a two-part enforcement surface: (1) an RBAC v2 attribute whitelist "shield" that restricts which token attributes may be used in privilege decisions (reduces operator blast radius and mitigates attribute injection risks), and (2) a lightweight KMS context prober that validates KMS usage context (region, provider, tenant hint) during policy evaluation to support region pinning and residency audits.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds an attribute whitelist compiler and admission-time enforcement hook for RBAC v2; policies can opt-in to deny decisions if unknown attributes are present.
- Implements a KMS context prober that queries the configured KMS adapter for metadata (region, key-tag) during policy evaluation without performing crypto operations (read-only metadata path).
- Adds an audit pseudonymizer that can be enabled per-tenant to redact high-cardinality PII (user and tenant identifiers) while preserving provenance hashes for troubleshooting.
- Provides migration tooling to map a small subset of long-form attribute names from legacy RBAC v1 rules into the stricter v2 whitelist schema.
- Ships unit and integration tests plus an optional Helm values flag and an installer hook for Private deployments.

Why not a simpler change?
- We intentionally split enforcement from metadata probing to avoid coupling crypto calls to the decision path; probes are cached for short TTLs and can be configured to favor safety or freshness.
- Pseudonymization targets audit export downstreams (S3/Cloud) where compliance teams want tokenized but linkable evidence.

Migration notes and rollout plan:
- Default behavior is opt-in. Existing policies are not changed automatically. Admins can run the provided migrate_rbac_v1_to_v2.sh to generate suggested whitelist manifests.
- The KMS prober is behind a feature flag (security.kms_context_prober.enabled=false by default) to allow staged rollout to Dedicated/Private customers.
- The audit pseudonymizer is a per-tenant toggle in the account settings API.

Testing and verification summary:
- Unit tests for attribute compiler and prober code paths.
- Integration test that spins up a local fake-kms adapter and validates region-mismatch denial policy.
- Smoke test verifying audit payload shape vs older exporter when pseudonymization enabled.

Files touched (high level):
- rbac/compiler/attribute_whitelist.go (new compiler and policy validator)
- k8s/admission/attribute_enforcer_webhook.go (admission webhook and controller wiring)
- infra/kms/prober/prober.go (read-only metadata probe)
- audit/serializer/pseudonymizer.go (pseudonymization strategy + config)
- installer/helm/templates/webhook-config.yaml (helm flag and RBAC rules)
- scripts/migrate_rbac_v1_to_v2.sh (migration helper)
- docs/security/attribute-whitelist.md (operator documentation and examples)

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added 
- [x] Integration tests added 
- [x] Security reviewed: initial crypto review done (Sofia) 
- [x] Docs updated with config example and migration steps
- [x] Helm flag and installer hook included

Backwards compatibility:
- No policy changes by default; admins must opt in. The migration script only emits suggested whitelists and does not apply them.

Known limitations and follow-ups:
- The prober relies on KMS adapter metadata endpoints; some legacy KMS providers may not expose all tags — follow-up ticket (ENG-2248) to add fallback heuristics.
- Pseudonymizer currently uses HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-scoped salt; future work (SEC-82) will add HSM-backed salt rotation for stronger forward secrecy.

review_comments: Amit Rao: Nice separation of concerns. Please add metrics for probe cache hit/miss and policy denials caused by unknown attributes.
Mariana Cortez: Added probe.cache_hit and rbac.whitelist_denials counters in infra/kms/prober and rbac/compiler. Also updated tests to assert counters where applicable.
Sofia Nguyen: Crypto review: ensure pseudonymizer uses tenant-scoped salt that is rotated. Salt storage must not be in plaintext. We should document rotation steps.

Mariana Cortez: Pseudonymizer uses HMAC with salt stored via KMS-wrapped secret (installer will configure KMS key). Added docs and integration smoke test that validates rotation can be signaled via admin API.
Liam O'Connor: Helm template: missing RBAC verbs for the admission controller; CI lint flagged it. Also tighten the PSP to disallow hostNetwork.
Mariana Cortez: Updated helm template and added PSP check. Reran linter locally and pushed fix. CI lint now passes.

merge_outcome: Merged by Sofia Nguyen via squash-merge. Commit message: "security: attribute whitelist shield + kms context prober; opt-in enforcement and audit pseudonymizer". Changelog: minor security feature, opt-in. Release note attached.
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in RBAC v2 attribute whitelist enforcement and a KMS metadata prober to help with region pinning and data residency audits. Adds audit pseudonymization for tenant PIIs (opt-in). Admins: see docs/security/attribute-whitelist.md for migration and rollout steps.
notes_for_ops: Operator: to enable KMS probing set security.kms_context_prober.enabled=true in values.yaml and ensure your KMS adapter exposes metadata tags. To enable audit pseudonymization toggle tenant setting and configure tenant-salt via the account API or KMS-wrapped secret. Monitor metrics rbac.whitelist_denials and probe.cache_hit to tune TTLs.
security_review_outcome: Initial crypto review completed by Sofia Nguyen; recommended HSM-backed salt rotation in follow-up (SEC-82). No blockers for opt-in rollout.
manual_steps_after_merge: 1) Communicate opt-in flags to enterprise customers. 2) Run scripts/migrate_rbac_v1_to_v2.sh in dry-run mode to review suggested whitelists. 3) If enabling pseudonymizer, provision tenant salt via installer and run smoke exporter tests.
